judged_text: The public members endpoint accepts an unbounded limit param — (params[:limit] || 50).to_i has no maximum — and applies it before serialization with no cap. Any user who can see a group can pass limit=100000000 and force the server to load and serialize the entire membership in one response, exhausting memory/bandwidth on the request path; the new code is an improvement over the old no-limit non-automatic path, but the newly introduced cap mechanism still lacks an upper clamp.

Any user who can see a group can pass limit=100000000 and force the server to load and serialize the entire membership in one response, exhausting memory/bandwidth on the request path; the new code is an improvement over the old no-limit non-automatic path, but the newly introduced cap mechanism still lacks an upper clamp.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff introduces pagination parameters but does not clamp `limit`: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and then `group.users...limit(limit)` (with `total = group.users.count`). Any requester who can hit `/groups/:group_id/members` can pass an arbitrarily large `limit` and force the server to load and serialize a huge membership set in one response. While the default is now 50, the lack of a maximum is directly visible in the new code path and matches the finding’s DoS/memory/bandwidth concern.
